question: A product team is brainstorming new feature ideas and wants Claude to generate a wide range of genuinely different concepts rather than several variations on the same idea. What should the team do when providing example ideas in the prompt?
options: A) Include no examples at all so nothing biases the range of ideas produced
B) Include a small set of deliberately varied examples so Claude avoids one narrow pattern
C) Include just one example and ask Claude to generate close variations of it
D) Include many examples that all follow the exact same structure as just one clear pattern
correct_answers: B) Include a small set of deliberately varied examples so Claude avoids one narrow pattern
explanations: Incorrect. While examples aren't required, omitting them does not itself guarantee variety; well-chosen diverse examples are the recommended way to actively support a broad range of ideas.
Correct. Examples should be diverse, covering edge cases and varying enough that Claude does not pick up an unintended narrow pattern, which supports a wide range of brainstormed ideas.
Incorrect. Asking for close variations of one example directly narrows the output to minor tweaks instead of a wide range of distinct ideas.
Incorrect. Uniform examples that all share the same structure and theme encourage Claude to converge on that single pattern rather than exploring genuinely different concepts.
